headline: Kody Clemens walks off Rays with two-out single
recap: Kody Clemens lined a two-out, bases-loaded single to right field in the bottom of the ninth, scoring Bryce Harper from third and lifting the Phillies to a 2-1 win over the Tampa Bay Rays. Brandon Lowe had tied the game in the top of the ninth with a solo home run off Carlos Estévez, but Garrett Cleavinger walked Buddy Kennedy to load the bases before Clemens delivered the winning hit.

Cristopher Sánchez started for Philadelphia and worked six scoreless innings, allowing four hits and a walk while striking out four. Tampa Bay used an opener plan, with Cole Sulser working the first inning before Tyler Alexander followed with four and a third innings in relief.

Kyle Schwarber's 34th home run of the season, a fly ball to right-center off Alexander in the sixth, had given the Phillies a 1-0 lead. Estévez, despite allowing Lowe's game-tying homer in the ninth for his fifth blown save of the season, picked up the win.
